title: fix(app-shell): Studio's field inspector closes on a view switch or Escape, and a read-only package reads as read-only (objectui#11781)
body:
Fixes #11781

Clause-②: no

## What changes

- **The field inspector belongs to the view that opened it.** In Studio's Data pillar, the *Field properties* rail now closes when the author switches view: Records, Form, or Advanced (Validations, Hooks, Actions, API, Settings). That is the same act as its own Close button. Re-selecting the view you are already on keeps it open.
- **Escape closes it too.** It closes only on an Escape that nothing inside the rail already answered. A Radix menu, select or dialog, the CEL autocomplete, the object picker and the grid's inline edits all call `preventDefault` on their own Escape. The keystroke must also come from inside the Data pillar, or from the page body, which is where focus lands after a click on the form preview. An Escape typed in another surface, such as the copilot dock, leaves the rail open.
- **A read-only package reads as read-only.**
  - The Form view's layout caption says *Read-only layout*, not *Draft layout*.
  - The form designer's hint says the package is read-only and that a click shows a field's properties.
  - The Access pillar's banner says the package's objects are read-only. It is a muted chip, not the amber *saved as draft*, and its tooltip says the permission sets can be viewed but not changed.
  - Writable packages are unchanged.
- **The validation editor looks disabled when it is.** On a read-only package, the Validations editor's inputs, selects and JSON boxes now wear the disabled look of the field inspector's inputs. Before, they kept the editable white fill and dark text.

The new copy is five rows in the metadata-admin designer table, in both EN and ZH. Each row describes what a read-only package *is*:

- `engine.studio.data.form.layoutBadgeReadOnly`
- `engine.studio.designer.hintReadOnly`
- `engine.studio.designer.fieldAriaReadOnly`
- `engine.studio.access.bannerReadOnly`
- `engine.studio.access.bannerTitleReadOnly`

No export, prop, type member or `packages/i18n` key is added.

## The dispatch's mechanism hypotheses, measured on main

- **H1, confirmed.** The selection is `DataPillar`'s `fieldSel` state. The right rail renders whenever `current && fieldSel && objLoaded` holds, whatever `viewMode` is. The segmented control and the Advanced menu called `setViewMode` and nothing else. They now call `selectViewMode`, which clears `fieldSel` when the view actually changes. The draft-object grid placeholder's *Go to Form · Layout* button goes through it as well.
- **Escape, in reach.** Escape acts on the same state (`fieldSel`), so it is in reach. The view-switch change alone does not cover it: no key handler read it at all. It needed its own document `keydown` listener. The listener is mounted only while the rail is open, and it is scoped as described above.
- **H2, half falsified.**
  - `AccessPillar` already receives the read-only signal: the surface's pillar switch renders it with `readOnly={readOnly}`. Nothing had to be threaded. Only the banner ignored the signal.
  - In the Form caption, `readOnly` was in scope. The caption fell through to `layoutBadgeClean`. It now asks `readOnly` first.
- **H3, confirmed and narrowed.**
  - The greyed inspector's text and select inputs are the `@object-ui/components` primitives `Input` and `SelectTrigger`, reached through `InspectorTextField` and `InspectorSelectField`. Their class lists carry `disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50`.
  - `ObjectValidationsPanel` uses plain elements, and Tailwind preflight keeps their editable colours when they are disabled. The panel now gives its twelve text-like controls that same pair, through one module constant, `DISABLED_LOOK`.
  - Plain checkboxes are left to the browser's own disabled look, as the inspector's own checkboxes are.
  - No primitive under `packages/components/src/ui/` is touched.

## One in-place repair under the bounded exemption

The form designer's field cards had the same defect as the hint they sit under. On a read-only package, each card still announced *click to edit properties, drag to reorder* to a screen reader, and showed a grab cursor and a drag handle. `SortableField` now takes the designer's `readOnly`:

- its accessible name uses `engine.studio.designer.fieldAriaReadOnly`;
- it shows a pointer cursor instead of the grab cursor;
- the drag handle is not drawn.

The exemption's four conditions hold:

- It is the same defect class.
- The fix is mechanical: one prop, branched the way the hint is.
- `ObjectFormDesigner.tsx` is on this claim's surface, and no other claim holds it.
- It falls under the same gate family.

The pin is in the read-only and writable cases of `StudioDesignSurface.readOnlyWording-11781.test.tsx`.

## Tests

New pins:

- `DataPillar.inspectorBelongsToView-11781.test.tsx` covers these cases:
  - switching from Form to each of the five Advanced views and to Records closes the rail;
  - Escape closes it;
  - control: re-clicking the open view keeps it;
  - control: an Escape that a capture-phase document listener already answered (the shape of a Radix layer) keeps it;
  - control: an Escape on an element outside the pillar keeps it.
- `StudioDesignSurface.readOnlyWording-11781.test.tsx` covers the read-only Form caption, the designer hint and the field card, and the Access banner and its tooltip. Each case has its writable control.
  - The wording is pinned by **key**, resolved through the table, so a copy edit does not turn it red. A missing row does turn it red, because `t` echoes the key back.
  - The writable controls read absent rows with plain `t`, so they pin only the unchanged half.
- `ObjectValidationsPanel.readOnlyLook-11781.test.tsx` covers format, state-machine and JSON-schema rules. On a read-only package, every text-like control is disabled and carries each `disabled:` utility of the shared `Input` primitive. The test reads those utilities from the primitive at run time and does not restate them. Control: the same controls are enabled when writable.

Updated: `DataPillar.layoutBadge.test.tsx` (objectui#4036's pin). Its read-only case asserted `Draft layout`, which is exactly this card's defect. It now asserts that no draft caption appears. Its helper waits on the pressed *Layout* control, not on the caption text.

**Reverse verification.** The run was made from commit `1edac01`, with the tests from HEAD. The four implementation files were checked out from the dispatch-era base `57dbe34`. For the three component files that base is byte-identical to the dispatch base `1e1f09e`. For `i18n.ts` it differs only by rows that objectui#11840 added.

- On-disk markers after the mutation were all 0: `selectViewMode`, the `layoutBadgeReadOnly` and `bannerReadOnly` uses, `hintReadOnly`, `DISABLED_LOOK` and the `layoutBadgeReadOnly` row.
- Result: `Tests 13 failed | 10 passed (23)`. Every defect pin turned red, and every control and precondition stayed green. The red direction was the expected one.
- After the restore, `git diff HEAD` was empty and all four blob hashes equalled HEAD. The script restored through a `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

## Gates

All gates below were run at HEAD `c9d5a3e` after the final merge of main, unless a line says otherwise. Every listed gate exited 0.

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `8 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`: `Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (3300 keys)`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-drift`: `No designer-table en value changed in this range`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-designer-parity`: `Every en row has a zh row, and every shared row carries the same placeholders`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys`: report only. None of the five new keys is listed.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: `OK (scanned 7854 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)`.
- The vi.mock gates (`check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`): each printed `OK`.
- The changeset gates (`check-changeset-no-major`, `-fixed`, `-overwrite`, `-claims`): each printed its `✅` line.
- `check-test-path-roots` and `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources`: `OK`.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the eight touched files: 0 errors and 15 warnings. For each of the four implementation files, the rule/message multiset is identical to `origin/main`'s, compared through `--stdin --stdin-filename`. The four test files have 0 warnings.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, run after a build of the dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`: `28 successful, 28 total`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly`, run at `02c06ec` (before the merges, with the same tsconfig and the same test files), lists all four touched test files.
- `pnpm exec vitest run`, from the repo root, over the 4 touched test files plus 5 neighbours (`DataPillar.celGate`, `DataPillar.panelGate`, `ObjectFormDesigner`, `ObjectValidationsPanel`, `StudioDesignSurface.accessGuard`): `Test Files 9 passed (9)`, `Tests 60 passed (60)`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/`, all files, at `9971f86` (the previous merge of main): 101 files and 635 tests passed, run in three foreground chunks. At `a77beaa`: 100 files and 615 tests passed.
- The 18 tests outside that directory that read the changed files (`i18n.ts` readers, the `ConditionBuilder` mount-scope pins, the i18n gate self-tests and others) passed at `9971f86`: 18 files, 552 tests.
- NOT MEASURED: `check-eager-locale-catalogues`. Reason: `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, because it reads a built console bundle. This change adds no locale-pack key.
- NOT MEASURED: a browser run against the showcase. The changes are covered by the DOM pins above. CI and review own the visual pass.

## Risk and cost

- **A faulty field formula.** Leaving the view now closes the inspector. The inspector's blocking count expires with its selection, by design, so the autosave may then send the draft. That is the same outcome as pressing Close: the ruled "sub-decision A" pinned in `DataPillar.celGate.test.tsx`, which keeps a closed rail from wedging Save shut. Before this change, the rail stayed open on Validations and kept the hold. The hold then expired the same way as soon as the author closed it.
- **Escape.** A layer inside the pillar that answers Escape without calling `preventDefault` would now also close the rail. Every Escape consumer measured on this path calls it.
- **Rollback:** revert the squash commit. No data, contract or export is involved.

## Acceptance notes: same family, not changed here

None of these is filed. Each is a reading of the source, not a reproduction, so none meets a filing class.

- `ObjectSettingsPanel` (Advanced → Settings) builds its selects and inputs from plain elements with no `disabled:` utilities. On a read-only package they should show the same editable look this PR removes from Validations. The file is outside this claim. Carrier: none.
- The Records grid's per-column edit button is labelled `engine.studio.data.editFieldProps` (*Edit field properties*) on a read-only package too. It lives in another region of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, which other claims also hold, so the bounded exemption's third condition fails. Carrier: none.
- An empty declared group in the form designer still says *Drag fields here* on a read-only package. Carrier: none.
- `ObjectFieldInspector`'s own `TextareaField` (the Description box) is a plain textarea with no `disabled:` utilities, so the "greyed" inspector is not fully greyed. Carrier: none.

## Overlap with in-flight work

This branch merged `origin/main` three times, most recently at `4e7dd56`. That brought in the Studio siblings: objectui#11790 (nav editor), objectui#11785 (error strips) and objectui#11792 (New package and New object). All merged without conflict. Each shares `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `i18n.ts` with this branch, in disjoint regions and under its own key prefixes.
